scenes.purpose: Open on the goal-to-workflow framing, attributed to MiniMax, and hold it long enough to read.
Fill the frame with the real supplied MiniMax Code interface on a display, so the product material reads as the hero rather than a small inset.
Present the three confirmed product-described capabilities as larger, shorter cards, labelled as MiniMax's description rather than measured results.
Hold the supplied CTA and URL to the final frame.

treatment.continuity: One white surface with ink type and MiniMax blue accents runs through every scene, so the title, the real screenshot and the cards read as one space. Each transition overlaps the outgoing scene by its transition length. The hook frames a goal; the display scene gives the real MiniMax Code window the whole frame; the feature grid lays out what MiniMax says the product does; the end card closes on the supplied CTA. Every capability line is attributed to MiniMax, and the grid header states that no measured results are shown.

holds.reason: Hook headline and attribution hold for reading before the crossfade.
Product display settles with a clean, large view of the real interface.
Three feature cards and the claim label stay readable after the stagger.
CTA and URL hold to the end.

treatment.message: MiniMax Code, as MiniMax describes it: Coding and Work modes, agents that team up on tasks, and tools for images, video, audio, scripts and voiceovers. These are product claims, not measured results.
